translationRepairs: In the fourth year of the Yuanyan era (12 BCE), he came to court accompanied by his entire retinue: his tutor, chancellor, and commandant.
In the fourth year of the Yuanyan era (9 BCE), he came to court accompanied by his entire retinue: his tutor, chancellor, and commandant.
元延四年 is Yuanyan year 4; with Yuanyan 1 = 12 BCE, year 4 is 9 BCE, so the parenthetical (12 BCE) is a conversion error and the proposed (9 BCE) is correct.
He enfeoffed his maternal uncle Ding Ming as Marquis of Yang'an, and Ding Ming's son Man as Marquis of Pingzhou.
He enfeoffed his maternal uncle Ding Ming as Marquis of Yang'an, and his maternal uncle's son Man as Marquis of Pingzhou.
舅子滿 means a maternal uncle's son Man, not Ding Ming's son; the next unit names Man's father as Zhong (忠), so the before text invents a false filiation that the proposal correctly removes.

In the eighth month, an imperial edict declared: 'Previously I commanded Xia Heliang and others to propose changing the reign title and extending the calendar periods, believing this would bring lasting stability to the nation.

In the eighth month, an imperial edict declared: 'Attendant-at-edict Xia Heliang and others proposed changing the reign title and extending the calendar periods, believing this would bring lasting stability to the nation.

Chapter 時詔 is a corrupt writing of the office 待詔/侍詔 (Attendant-at-edict); Yan Shigu's text emends （時）〔待〕詔, and reading it as 'I commanded' invents imperial agency the Chinese does not support. The proposed office-title rendering is accurate.

In the eighth month, an edict stated: 'At the time I ordered Xia Helang and others to propose changing the era name and designation, increasing the water clock periods, believing it could permanently secure the state.

In the eighth month, an edict stated: 'Attendant-at-edict Xia Helang and others proposed changing the era name and designation, increasing the water clock periods, believing it could permanently secure the state.
The literal's 'At the time I ordered' likewise misreads 時詔; critical editions restore 待詔 as Xia Heliang's office title, so Attendant-at-edict is the correct sense.

In the second month, he enfeoffed Imperial Grand Empress Dowager's younger cousin Chamberlain Fu Shang as Marquis of Ruchang, and Empress Dowager's uterine younger brother Chamberlain Zheng Ye as Marquis of Yangxin.

In the second month, he enfeoffed Imperial Grand Empress Dowager's younger cousin Chamberlain Fu Shang as Marquis of Ruchang, and the son of the Empress Dowager's uterine younger brother, Chamberlain Zheng Ye, as Marquis of Yangxin.
太后同母弟子侍中鄭業 means Zheng Ye is the son of the Empress Dowager's uterine younger brother; the before literal drops 子 and wrongly makes Zheng Ye that brother himself.
